articles.full_content:
Agricultural development, smarter farming and farmer empowerment are key to building a Viksit Bharat: PM The solar power revolution of the PM-KUSUM scheme has transformed the country's Annadatas into Urjadatas : PM We move forward with the concept of 'Lab to Land': PM Namo Drone Didis are demonstrating how advanced technology can be effectively used in village: PM India offers growing opportunities in everything from agri-engineering to agri-startups. The focus is on empowering farmers to become agricultural entrepreneurs: PM
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026. Addressing the gathering on the occasion in the presence of agricultural scientists, agri-entrepreneurs, and farmers from across the nation, the Prime Minister commended the media group for its enthusiastic past participation in the cleanliness campaign and for dedicating two full days to organizing this innovative Kisan Mela.
Noting that the conference is taking place amid a festive atmosphere just days after Deepavali and during the ongoing Chhath Mahaparv, which is deeply rooted in agrarian life, the Prime Minister pointed out that major Indian festivals such as Bihu, Pongal, Onam, Baisakhi, Sarhul, and Pola are intrinsically tied to farming. “Meaning, agriculture and farming are our culture, our tradition, and the foundation of our social life,” observed PM Modi.
Recalling his Red Fort address on the seven streams of national strength (Saptadhara) required for a Viksit Bharat, in which agriculture serves as a primary pillar, the Prime Minister emphasized that the significance of such farmer conferences has grown manifold because national development depends directly on agricultural modernization. “The building of a Viksit Bharat is simply not possible without developing agriculture, without making farming smarter, and without empowering the farmer,” asserted Shri Modi.
Illustrating the close link between agricultural growth and national progress through a widely discussed World Bank study showing that 50 crore Indians escaped poverty in just 12 to 13 years with a sharp decline in rural poverty among small farmers and farm laborers, the Prime Minister highlighted that this period coincided with India's agriculture sector achieving an average growth rate above 4 percent for the first decade since independence.
Observing that farmers and agricultural experts understand the necessity of continuous policy and methodological evolution, the Prime Minister pointed out that as global markets, dietary habits, weather patterns, and technologies evolved over time, farmers needed to be empowered afresh. “Merely filling the granaries of food grains is not enough,” asserted Shri Modi.

NITI Aayog Launches Report on “Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes”
articles.full_content:
NITI Aayog today released the report titled “Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes”, prepared in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad as the knowledge partner. The report recognizes the PLI Scheme as a flagship policy intervention launched by the Government of India to enhance India’s manufacturing competitiveness, integrate Indian firms into global value chains, and accelerate the journey towards an Atmanirbhar Bharat. By providing production-linked incentives to a select set of high-performing firms, the scheme is designed to be self-sustaining, encouraging adoption of advanced technologies, capacity creation, and sustained growth in output and exports.
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes, implemented by various Ministries and Departments, have emerged as a successful initiative for scaling up domestic manufacturing, investment and production, while strengthening India’s position in global value chains by driving exports, building domestic capabilities and enhancing competitiveness. Acting as a catalyst for industrial deepening, employment and export expansion, the initiative is advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 through a globally competitive manufacturing sector.
The report presents a sector-wise assessment of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme across all 14 sectors notified by the Government of India, examining its impact on the key parameters of investment, additional production, exports, and employment generation. The assessment is based on sector-wise collection of firm-level data shared by implementing Ministries, supplemented by industry-level inputs from authenticated sources. Sectoral outcomes have been categorized into four broad groups: On-Track, Partial Impact, Insignificant Evidence of Impact, and Data unavailable; providing a structured and comparative overview of the scheme’s progress across sectors.
The report finds that sectors with strong industry participation have demonstrated encouraging outcomes under the scheme. Pharmaceuticals, Mobile Manufacturing under Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM), Food Processing, Telecom, White Goods, Automobiles and Drones have shown notable progress in investment, production and capacity creation, with the Drones sector emerging as an early implementation success.
Manufacturing capacity in High Efficiency Solar PV Modules has also expanded significantly, reflecting growing domestic capability and strengthening India’s renewable energy manufacturing ecosystem. The report further notes that sectors involving advanced and emerging technologies such as ACC Batteries, Specialty Steel and Technical Textiles are witnessing gradual capacity creation and ecosystem development, which are expected to contribute significantly to India’s long-term industrial growth trajectory. Across sectors, the scheme has played an important role in stimulating investment, enhancing manufacturing capacity and strengthening industrial competitiveness.

NSO appeals for public cooperation in Socio-Economic Surveys across Assam
articles.full_content:
The Field Operations Division (FOD) of the National Statistics Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, is conducting large-scale socio-economic surveys across India including selected locations in Assam.
The surveys are aimed at collecting primary data on a wide range of socio-economic indicators, including household income, migration, debt and investment, employment, agriculture and industries.
The Regional Office, Guwahati, and the Sub-Regional Office, Silchar, will undertake the survey work at various locations during November 2026 under the districts Dhubri, Bajali, Baksa, Barpeta, Bongaigaon Chirang, Goalpara, Kamrup (R), Kamrup(M), Kokrajhar, Nalbari, South Salmara Mankachar, Tamulpur, Cachar, Dima Hasao, Karbi Anglong, Sribhumi(Karimganj), Hailakandi and West Karbi Anglong. As part of the survey process, field officials will visit selected households and establishments to collect information us her here e ing scientifically designed survey schedules.
Appealing for public support, the Director and Regional Head, NSO (FOD), Regional Office, Guwahati, has requested citizens to extend full cooperation to the authorised officers and officials during the survey period by providing accurate and complete information. Such cooperation will help to generate reliable official statistics that are crucial for informed policy formulation and nation building.
The NSO has assured that all information collected during the surveys will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for statistical purposes.
The tentative schedule of visits by officials of the NSO (FOD) for conducting surveys during November 2026 is available here .

DGFT prohibits export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass to strengthen domestic recycling and critical mineral recovery
articles.full_content:
The measure aims to ensure domestic availability of critical minerals, strengthen battery recycling capacity and reduce import dependence Measure to complement Government’s ₹1,500 crore Incentive Scheme for Critical Mineral Recycling
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Department of Commerce, has prohibited the export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass falling under ITC(HS) Code 85491400. Vide Notification No. 49/2026-27 dated 10 November 2026, the export policy of the item has been amended from ‘Free’ to ‘Prohibited’ with immediate effect and until further orders. The transitional arrangements under Para 1.05 of the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP), 2023, will apply.
ITC(HS) Code 85491400 covers waste and scrap of primary cells, primary batteries and electric accumulators, as well as spent cells, batteries and accumulators, which are unsorted and do not contain lead, cadmium or mercury. The Notification specifically describes the item as Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass. Black Mass is the powdery material obtained from shredding end-of-life lithium-ion batteries and battery manufacturing waste. It contains recoverable quantities of critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese.
Critical minerals are essential inputs for electric mobility, advanced chemistry cell batteries, energy storage, electronics and renewable energy. India depends substantially on imports for several of these minerals. Recycling battery waste is among the quickest and most sustainable ways of developing a domestic supply of these resources. While the country's capacity to recycle battery waste and refine critical minerals from it has grown considerably, it is not being fully utilised due to inadequate feedstock availability. Exports of Black Mass generated in India divert this valuable secondary resource abroad, while domestic recyclers have, in some cases, had to import material to meet their requirements.
The export prohibition is intended to ensure that Black Mass generated in India is recycled and refined within the country. The measure is expected to assure feedstock availability for domestic recycling and refining units, improve their capacity utilisation and encourage further investment and employment in the sector. It will increase domestic recovery of lithium, cobalt, nickel and other critical minerals, thereby reducing import dependence and the associated foreign exchange outgo. It will also strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing, electric vehicles, energy storage and clean-energy technologies, in line with the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Further, the measure will advance the circular economy and ‘urban mining’, reducing reliance on primary mining, while supporting environmentally sound recycling of this hazardous material within the country in accordance with applicable environmental regulations.
